classification: measure with an explicit finite joint prior; standard chain-rule and conditional-DPI consequences with distinguishing vectors, not a new universal lineage law
quantity: Delta(Y|S)=I(T;Y|S)=H(T|S)-H(T|S,Y). Both orders use the identical full joint law, truth variable, prior, source identities and domain. The selected observation is the full tuple, not an aggregated majority value.
scope: Finite named alphabets and rational joint probabilities normalized exactly to one; bits use the existing binary64-log2 approximation. These are model quantities, not certified empirical mutual-information estimates.

knownIdentities.statement: Delta>=0; Delta=0 iff T and Y are conditionally independent given S, under the declared joint law.
knownIdentities.classification: standard Shannon identity and nonnegativity; finite vectors here, no new Lean formalization

knownIdentities.statement: For any complete addition order, the sum of marginals is I(T;all sources). The sum is invariant, while individual attribution may depend on order.
knownIdentities.classification: chain rule; no permutation of attributed acts or history is performed

knownIdentities.statement: An exact copy determined by S has zero marginal information. Another source has strictly greater gain only when its conditional information is positive.
knownIdentities.classification: conditional consequence, not a rule inferred from lineage labels

comparison.sufficientHypothesis: For the same prior and previous tuple S, require T -> (S,Y_other) -> Y_same, equivalently I(T;Y_same|S,Y_other)=0. This is a conditional garbling/order assumption; distinct lineage or equal prediction accuracy does not establish it.
comparison.conclusion: I(T;Y_same|S)<=I(T;Y_other|S). Strictness additionally requires a positive information difference; it is not automatic.
comparison.argument: Expand I(T;Y_same,Y_other|S) in both orders. Under the stated conditional independence the expansion beginning with Y_other ends at I(T;Y_other|S). The other expansion adds a nonnegative term to I(T;Y_same|S).
comparison.vectorCheck: The candidate reader verifies the conditional-independence hypothesis by exact rational factorization of the handed finite table; it does not infer causal lineages.

existingImplementation: Reuse published mixProjectionLoss on configurations (truth, selected tuple), with zero weight on truth and unit weight on tuple. Its conditional configuration loss is exactly H(truth|tuple). No entropy engine, causal generator or algebra is replaced.

counterexamples.result: All three sources have accuracy 1/2 and individual information 1 bit. After the first source, the same-lineage complementary projection adds 1 bit while the other-lineage redundant projection adds 0. A comparable marginal quality is insufficient; the missing condition concerns joint conditional information.
After a perfect report, a noiseless report from a distinct declared lineage adds zero, so no universal strict ranking holds.
Each masked view alone has zero truth information; after one view the other adds a bit. Mutual-information gains need not have diminishing returns without additional hypotheses.

The full tuple preserves the perfect first report. The existing weighted mix becomes constant after two constant-zero reports and loses a bit. That loss is not negative conditional mutual information.

validation: Missing joint/prior is unmeasured; nonnormalized priors, invalid domains and orders that are not permutations refuse by name. Every prefix is projected from the same complete joint table; no defaults, resampling, inferred independence or truth-free estimation is supplied.
cache: Only scalar subset readings are cached by an explicitly named set-of-coordinates key. This sorts neither the handed addition orders nor their attributed history; probabilities and atom IDs remain intact.
numeric: Exact rational masses; approximate bits, default vector tolerance 1e-12. Raw floating-point residuals are retained, never clamped to zero to claim a law.

literature.addsHere: One-joint two-order vectors, an exact finite check of the comparison hypothesis, and counterexamples to lineage-only ranking; no new Shannon inequality.
